name: TS5A3159DCKR
title: 1 Ω SPDT analog switch, 1.65 V to 5.5 V
summary: A single-pole double-throw CMOS analog switch for one supply from 1.65 V to 5.5 V. COM goes to NC with IN low and to NO with IN high, breaking one path before making the other. On resistance is 0.75 Ω typical at 4.5 V, matched to 0.1 Ω between channels, with low charge injection and THD; the control input tolerates 5.5 V at any supply. Six-pin SOT-23 (DBV) and SC70 (DCK).
key_figures: 0.75 Ω typ, 1.1 Ω max at V+ = 4.5 V

notes: A marking in parentheses lists alternatives separated by commas; one of them appears on a part.

circuits.title: System schematic
circuits.description: A controller selects which of two system lines reaches its own signal pin. One GPIO drives IN, held low by a resistor to ground so COM rests on NC; a second controller line joins COM, and NO and NC run out to the system. Signals pass in either direction. V+ comes from a 5 V rail with a capacitor to ground at the pin.

parts.note: size set by GPIO drive, power and switching rate

notes: V+ is 1.8 V in the design example; any supply in the recommended range may be used.
With an open-drain GPIO, R1 is a pull-up.

circuits.title: Turnon and turnoff time
circuits.description: COM is held at VCOM = V+. Each of NC and NO carries its own load of RL = 50 Ω and CL = 35 pF to ground. A logic pulse on IN switches the path; tON and tOFF run from the 50 % point of the control edge to the 90 % point of the switch output.

parts.note: PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr < 5 ns, tf < 5 ns

circuits.title: Break-before-make time
circuits.description: NC and NO are tied to one source at V+/2. COM drives RL = 50 Ω and CL = 35 pF to ground. When IN changes state the output dips while neither path conducts; tBBM is the time the output spends below 90 % of its level.

parts.note: PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr < 5 ns, tf < 5 ns

circuits.title: Charge injection
circuits.description: A DC source VGEN, swept from 0 to V+, feeds one switch port through RGEN = 0. COM drives only CL to ground. IN is pulsed off, on and off; the step left on VCOM times CL is the injected charge.

parts.note: PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr < 5 ns, tf < 5 ns

notes: The charge-injection fixture lists CL = 0.1 nF; the electrical characteristics list CL = 1 nF.
The driven port may be NC or NO.

circuits.title: Total harmonic distortion
circuits.description: A source of V+ peak to peak, 600 Hz to 20 kHz, loaded by RL = 600 Ω, reaches COM through 10 µF. The path is set COM to NC. NC carries CL = 50 pF to ground and RL = 600 Ω to V+/2, and feeds the analyzer through a second 10 µF.

equations.note: Channel ON, VI = VIH or VIL.

where.ΔVCOM: step on the output caused by switching IN

operation.text: One pole, two throws, conducting in both directions. With IN low COM joins NC; with IN high COM joins NO. NC is the normally closed port and NO the normally open one.

On a change of IN the closed path opens before the other one closes, so NC and NO are never joined through COM. Minimum tBBM is 1 ns at every supply, except 0.5 ns over temperature in the 1.8-V electrical characteristics.

Signals from 0 V to V+ pass in either direction on a single 1.65 V to 5.5 V supply. Low ron, ron matching, charge injection and THD keep distortion low. Listed uses: mobile phones, consumer and computing equipment, portable instrumentation and portable audio.
IN accepts 0 V to 5.5 V at any V+. IN must be driven high or low: a floating or mid-threshold input partly turns on the input transistors, raising supply current and leaving the switch state unknown.

IN defaults low through a pull-down resistor. Its value is a trade between the GPIO's drive strength, power drawn and the switching rate; an open-drain GPIO takes a pull-up. A decoupling capacitor goes on V+.

V+ may be any voltage in the recommended range. A single-supply device takes a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor as close to the supply pin as possible; 0.1 µF and 1 µF are often paralleled to cover different noise frequencies.
NO, NC or COM that are not used may float or go to GND. IN may not float.

At a 90° trace corner the trace is 1.414 times wider at the apex; the change in distributed capacitance and self-inductance causes a reflection. A chamfered corner (chamfer about 2W across, at least 1W of trace at the inside) is better, and a rounded corner of constant width is best.
Latch-up performance above 100 mA per JESD 78 Class II. ESD tested to JESD 22: 2000 V human-body model (A114-B, Class II), 1000 V charged-device model (C101).

rpeak is the largest ron across the stated range; Δron is the ron difference between the two channels; ron(flat) is the spread between highest and lowest ron of one channel over the stated conditions. Off leakage is taken at NC or NO with that path open; on leakage at NC or NO with the path closed and COM open, or at COM with NC or NO open. tON, tOFF and tBBM are delays from the IN edge to the analog outputs. BW is the frequency where a closed path falls 3 dB below its DC gain. OFF isolation and crosstalk are in dB at a given frequency, crosstalk being coupling from a closed path to the open one. I+ is supply current with IN at V+ or GND; ΔI+ is the rise in I+ for each control input held at a given voltage instead.
TS5A3159-Q1 is an automotive Q100-qualified version and TS5A3159-EP an enhanced-product version.
